turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, Mr Pillay is in. I got a pressure of 148 over 86 and a pulse of 74 just now. File's on your desk.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come in. Sit down. What is it?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for fitting me in. I have come about cramps in my calves at night.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Two months now, doctor. Umm, almost every night. They wake me. Both calves, though the right is the worse one.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm Leah, his daughter. I hear him from the passage when it starts. We were late, sorry, the robots were out.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. None.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Not that either, doctor.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight going up or down?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I couldn't really say, doctor. Um, I have not been keeping track.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): A water tablet, doctor. Furoseamide, uh, 40 milligrams, one every morning. I have had high blood pressure for many years, and the tablet is for that.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm not sure it's every morning, doctor. Some days the tablet is still sitting there when he leaves.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I believe I take it as I was instructed, doctor. I do not mean to miss it.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything from the chemist?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. Magnesium, which I bought myself at the chemist. I think the strength is 250 milligrams, one at night, for the cramps. Err, I have used it for a few weeks.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much water in a day?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Very little, I am afraid. Two cups of tea and perhaps one glass of water. That is about all.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I pack a bottle and it comes home still full. Every time.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): With the blood pressure, any headaches?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes, doctor. A mild one, early in the morning. Not every day.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): While we're here, his grandson, my Kyle, made fifty at cricket on Saturday. You should have seen the boy's face.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): It was a lovely innings, yes. We sat in the sun the whole afternoon. The heat this week has been quite something, has it not?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja. Storms building over the Highveld too. I caught the Proteas on the radio driving in, that last over.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The drive back from the ground was worse than the robots this morning. If the bonus comes through we'll get him new pads.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): He has his eye on a bat as well. Gray-Nicolls, I think. Quite dear.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Legs.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Calves are soft. No tenderness, no swelling. Foot pulses are there, both sides.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think these are night cramps from the water tablet and not drinking enough. I can't rule out a low potassium until the bloods are back.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): I see. What do you suggest, doctor?

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll book bloods for the potassium and the kidney function. Stretch each calf before bed, hold it thirty seconds, both sides. Drink more water through the day. If the cramps have not settled we might do a scan of the legs, but not now.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I shall stretch, and I shall try to drink more. When ought I to come back?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks with the results. Sister will sort the form.
[SEG0036] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take you down to the lab, Mr Pillay, they can draw it this morning. Watch the step by the door.

spec.situation: Older person with calf cramps at night for two months; takes a water tablet; drinks little water; magnesium from the shop; blood tests for potassium planned; stretching advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
